title: 3 Powerful And Unique Ways To Model
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin argues that modeling is essential to engagement and behavior management, but warns that repeating the same modeling approach day after day bores students, and offers three techniques to keep it fresh. Detailed modeling means showing students not just the general action but the exact mechanics behind it, with rich narrative detail, since specificity itself is what interests students. Silent modeling means demonstrating an entire process without speaking a single word, which he says forces teachers to be more precise and demonstrative and mesmerizes students. Complex modeling means deliberately adding extra steps to routines that are otherwise too simple to hold students' attention, extending responsibility and challenge into everyday procedures like entering the classroom. He argues that all three techniques share the same underlying goal: making modeling more interesting and detailed increases engagement and reduces misbehavior, and that teachers should experiment with each rather than relying on the same tired routine.
points: Detailed modeling means demonstrating the specific mechanics of a task (like exact finger position on a paintbrush), not just the general action — details are what interest students.
Silent modeling — demonstrating an entire process without saying a word — forces a teacher to be more precise and mesmerizes students in the process.
Complex modeling means deliberately adding extra steps to routines that are too simple, extending responsibility and challenge into everyday procedures.
Repeating the same modeling approach day after day, like unchanged 'dance moves' used for 20 years, bores students and undercuts its effectiveness.
The better a teacher is at modeling, the more effective and successful both teacher and students become, with reduced misbehavior as a direct result.
quotes: Going a day without modeling is like gardening without a trowel.
You don’t just use a paintbrush, for example, you show your students how to hold it. You explain the finger position in relation to the ferrule while walking around the room and showing them.
Silent modeling forces you to be more demonstrative and mime-like. It forces you to be detailed, exacting, and right on target.

The way it works is that you’re going to add steps to boring routines. For example, instead of just entering the classroom in the morning and sitting down, you’re going to have them hang their backpacks in a certain way, check their mailboxes.
The idea is to extend your routines into more responsibility. Continue to add until your room runs like an atomic clock and you can focus solely on instruction.
Increase the challenge and interest in your classroom through modeling, and you’ll reduce misbehavior and captivate more and more of your students every day.
